A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FineXtract work. All 18 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–J, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original extraction experiments on WikiArt, DreamBooth and real-world checkpoints, plus caption extraction, ablations and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The model-guidance procedure, conditional correction term, graph-based clustering and Appendix A caption-extraction algorithm are unchanged. Wording and notation edits do not alter their operation.

E1.justification: Both retain WikiArt style extraction, DreamBooth object extraction, real-world checkpoints, mixed datasets and missing, extracted and extended-caption scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Direct Text2img plus clustering and CFG plus clustering retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. The caption experiments and model-guidance ablation also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Metrics, sample counts, model configurations and experimental protocols match. Both retain SSCD thresholds of 0.6 and 0.7, the default generation budget N = 50 × N0, the same guidance settings and the same appendix protocols.

E4.justification: The guidance-scale and correction-term ablations, sample-count analyses, preprocessing defenses, mixed-dataset studies and caption-related analyses are retained with the same evidence. Figure relocation does not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting and averaging descriptions. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted trends and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 7 retains FineXtract AS values of 0.501, 0.314 and 0.192 for full, extracted and empty captions, respectively.

T1.justification: The assumptions and derivations in Section 4 and Appendix A are retained. Section 4.2 changes q(x,c) to q(x|c) in a score expression; their log-gradients with respect to x coincide for fixed c, so this clarifies notation without changing the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: distribution-based model guidance, extraction through clustering, empirical applicability and extraction of about 20% of fine-tuning data in most cases.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning caption availability, guidance failures, the negative correction-term setting, clustering complexity, defense–quality tradeoffs and FLUX memory requirements.

D1.justification: Reported training settings, prompts, LoRA rank, caption-optimization details, hardware and timing information are unchanged. The PDFs also provide the same code, training-script and checkpoint access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to diffusion-model memorization, extraction, personalization and defenses.

P1.justification: v3 removes duplicated wording such as 'the the' and 'by omitting by omitting', corrects 'Abaltion' and 'hype-parameters', and slightly clarifies caption-conditioned distribution wording. Section order and the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 shrinks from a full-width display on page 5 to a single-column display on page 4. Figure 4 moves between columns on page 7, with accompanying text reflow, equation spacing and caption adjustments. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Small wording and notation corrections improve polish, while the reduced Figure 2 size makes its labels less legible at normal page scale. These localized presentation tradeoffs leave overall quality essentially unchanged; the methods, empirical support, limitations and reproducibility information remain the same.
